hooks.text: A classified military mirror is about to outscan the Hubble telescope.
NASA built a flagship telescope using a surplus spy satellite mirror.
Could a secret surveillance tool find the building blocks of life?

title: The Spy Mirror Hunting for Alien Worlds
description: NASA adapted a surplus spy satellite mirror to create the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, which sees 100 times more sky than Hubble.

beats.text: A classified military mirror is about to outscan the Hubble telescope.
beats.visual: artist's concept of the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope in deep space, 2020
queries: Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope artist concept

beats.text: In 2012, the National Reconnaissance Office surprised NASA by donating two 2.4-meter surveillance mirrors.
beats.visual: photograph of a 2.4-meter primary mirror for a telescope, 2012

beats.text: NASA's first chief of astronomy, Nancy Grace Roman, inspired the agency to repurpose one for a new mission.
beats.visual: NASA portrait of astronomer Nancy Grace Roman, 1960s

beats.text: Engineers adapted this reconnaissance hardware into a flagship observatory to solve the mysteries of dark energy.
beats.visual: clean room photo of the Roman Space Telescope assembly process
queries: Wide Field Instrument Roman Space Telescope

beats.text: On August 30, 2026, a SpaceX Falcon Heavy will carry this former spy tool to a point 1.5 million kilometers from Earth.
beats.visual: photograph of a SpaceX Falcon Heavy launching from Kennedy Space Center

beats.text: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope matches Hubble's resolution but captures an area 100 times larger.
beats.visual: split-screen graphic comparing Hubble's field of view with Roman's field of view
queries: Hubble vs Roman field of view comparison

beats.text: It is expected to scan more of the sky in five years than Hubble did in over thirty.
beats.visual: panoramic survey mosaic from the Hubble Space Telescope

beats.text: That incredible survey power stems entirely from recycling top-secret military hardware.
beats.visual: artist concept of gravitational microlensing detecting a planet in deep space
